target.title: fix: keep tail alive and replay timed-out messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A single Discord Gateway event handler error, recovered panic, or cooperative 30-second timeout was sent through the same fatal channel as worker-queue saturation. That terminated `discrawl tail` even though the Gateway session itself was healthy.

Keeping the tail alive exposed a second loss mode: a timed-out message can remain absent after the channel cursor advances beyond it. Ordinary forward repair then starts after that cursor and can never fetch the exact missed message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate fatal tail failures from event-scoped handler failures; queue saturation remains fail-fast.
- Carry safe event metadata through queued work and report handler errors, panics, and timeouts without terminating the tail.
- Preserve failed message identities in the durable failure ledger.
- On each repair tick, process a bounded least-recently-attempted set of unresolved `discord/tail_message` failures after ordinary forward repair.
- Fetch each candidate by exact channel/message ID, validate the returned identity, and persist through the canonical idempotent message upsert path.
- Advance channel cursors only through the existing monotonic API, without changing `tail:last_event` or appending synthetic `message_events`.
- Resolve the exact failure only after the durable upsert succeeds. Missing, inaccessible, mismatched, and retryable responses remain unresolved and rotate fairly through later bounded attempts.
- Resolve matching timeout failures when normal page sync independently writes those exact messages.
- Keep missing handlers, Gateway/session open failures, ready-hook failures, cancellation, worker bounds, publishing behavior, and shutdown behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Transient per-event failures no longer stop the live tail. If a failed message falls behind its channel cursor, hourly repair can recover that exact message without replaying channel history or duplicating Gateway events. Failures that cannot be positively recovered remain visible instead of being silently cleared.

Warnings and replay summaries contain identifiers and classifications only; they do not log message content, payloads, usernames, tokens, panic values, or raw secret-bearing errors.

## Evidence

Current head:

- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/store ./internal/syncer ./internal/discord`
- `go vet ./...`
- Focused tests cover below-cursor recovery, monotonic cursors, idempotence, no synthetic events, unchanged `tail:last_event`, bounded retry rotation, guild scope, normal-page resolution, inaccessible responses, and identity mismatches.

Initial continuation change also passed the repository CI, CodeQL, secret scanning, Docker, lint, release, dependency, and test checks on commit `daa933a`.
